title: AdaMerge: Tuning-Free Patch Compression for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2609.22562v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-vector visual document retrieval (VDR) models such as ColPali and ColNomic achieve strong accuracy by representing each document with hundreds to thousands of patch-level embeddings, at substantial storage and latency cost. Existing compression methods either prune unimportant patches or merge similar ones into clusters; the recent state-of-the-art merging method Prune-then-Merge (PtM) consistently outperforms pruning-only baselines at high compression, but requires a per-dataset cluster budget m to be tuned by grid search. We observe that the merge-cosine sequence produced by hierarchical clustering exhibits a sharp cliff separating mergeable redundancy from salient signal, and that the location of this cliff is concentrated in a narrow band across more than 11,000 documents from 14 datasets. This suggests the merge boundary can be detected per document rather than tuned per dataset. Building on this observation, we propose AdaM

translated_title: AdaMerge：面向多向量视觉文档检索的免调参补丁压缩方法
translated_abstract: arXiv:2609.22562v1 公告类型：cross。摘要：诸如 ColPali 和 ColNomic 等多向量视觉文档检索（VDR）模型通过为每个文档表示数百至数千个补丁级嵌入来实现很高的检索精度，但代价是巨大的存储和延迟开销。现有的压缩方法要么剪枝不重要的补丁，要么将相似的补丁合并成簇；最近最先进的合并方法 Prune-then-Merge（PtM）在高压缩率下始终优于仅剪枝的基线方法，但需要通过网格搜索为每个数据集调节聚类预算 m。我们观察到，层次聚类所产生的合并余弦序列呈现出一个急剧的“悬崖”，将可合并的冗余与显著信号清晰地区分开来，并且在来自 14 个数据集的 11,000 多个文档中，该悬崖的位置集中在一个狭窄的区间内。这表明合并边界可以针对每个文档进行检测，而无需针对每个数据集进行调参。基于这一观察，我们提出了 AdaM（erge）……
tldr: 提出了 AdaMerge，一种免调参的多向量视觉文档检索补丁压缩方法，它利用层次聚类合并余弦序列中普遍存在的“悬崖”边界，按文档自动区分可合并的冗余与关键信号，从而摆脱了现有最先进方法需要逐数据集网格搜索调参的限制。
en_tdlr: AdaMerge is a tuning-free patch compression method for multi-vector visual document retrieval that leverages a sharp, universally located "cliff" in the merge-cosine sequence of hierarchical clustering to automatically separate mergeable redundancy from salient signal per document, eliminating the need for per-dataset grid search tuning required by prior state-of-the-art methods.
